before.problem:
The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{2}{{t}^{2}+2}\cdot q(t).
$$

Find the principal normal vector at the point where $t=1$, if 

$$
\begin{aligned}q(1)=-i+j+\frac{1}{2}k,\,{q}^{′}(1)=j+k.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: The principal normal is N(1)=T′(1)/‖T′(1)‖. By the product rule, T′(1)=−(4/9)q(1)+(2/3)q′(1)=(4/9)i+(2/9)j+(4/9)k. Its magnitude is 2/3, so N(1)=(2/3)i+(1/3)j+(2/3)k.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{2}{{t}^{2}+2}\cdot q(t).
$$

Find the principal normal vector at the point where $t=1$, if 

$$
\begin{aligned}q(1)=-i+j+\frac{1}{2}k,\,{q}^{′}(1)=j+k.\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
First, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2}{{t}^{2}+2}\cdot q(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2}{{t}^{2}+2})\cdot q(t)+\frac{2}{{t}^{2}+2}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(q(t)) \\  & =-\frac{4t}{({t}^{2}+2)^{2}}\cdot q(t)+\frac{2}{{t}^{2}+2}\cdot {q}^{′}(t) \\  \\ {T}^{′}(1) & =-\frac{4(1)}{({1}^{2}+2)^{2}}\cdot q(1)+\frac{2}{{1}^{2}+2}\cdot {q}^{′}(1) \\  & =-\frac{4}{9}(-i+j+\frac{1}{2}k)+\frac{2}{3}(j+k) \\  & =\frac{4}{9}\,i+\frac{2}{9}\,j+\frac{4}{9}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(1)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{4}{9})}^{2}+{(\frac{2}{9})}^{2}+{(\frac{4}{9})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{16}{81}+\frac{4}{81}+\frac{16}{81}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{36}{81}} \\  & =\frac{6}{9} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(1)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve at the point where $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(1) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(1)}{‖{T}^{′}(1)‖} \\  & =\frac{\frac{4}{9}\,i+\frac{2}{9}\,j+\frac{4}{9}\,k}{(\frac{2}{3})} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\,i+\frac{1}{3}\,j+\frac{2}{3}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Note that when we find the scalar product of $T$ and $N$ at the point where $t=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1)\cdot N(1) & =\frac{2}{3}q(1)\cdot (\frac{2}{3}\,i+\frac{1}{3}\,j+\frac{2}{3}\,k) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}(-i+j+\frac{1}{2}k)\cdot (\frac{2}{3}\,i+\frac{1}{3}\,j+\frac{2}{3}\,k) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}(-\frac{2}{3}\,i\cdot \,i+\frac{1}{3}\,j\cdot j+\frac{1}{3}\,k\cdot k) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}(-\frac{2}{3}+\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{3}) \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given by T(t)=2t2+2⋅q(t). Find the principal normal vector at the point where t=1, if q(1)=−i+j+12k,q′(1)=j+k.

a

i

23i+13j+23k
d
33i+33j−33k
e

Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we calculate T′(t) and evaluate it at t=1:

T′(t)=ddt(2t2+2⋅q(t))=ddt(2t2+2)⋅q(t)+2t2+2⋅ddt(q(t))=−4t(t2+2)2⋅q(t)+2t2+2⋅q′(t)T′(1)=−4(1)(12+2)2⋅q(1)+212+2⋅q′(1)=−49(−i+j+12k)+23(j+k)=49i+29j+49k

Next, we find the magnitude of T′(1):

‖T′(1)‖=(49)2+(29)2+(49)2=1681+481+1681=3681=69=23

Finally, we normalize T′(1) and obtain the principal normal to the curve at the point where t=1:

N(1)=T′(1)‖T′(1)‖=49i+29j+49k(23)=23i+13j+23k

T(1)⋅N(1)=23q(1)⋅(23i+13j+23k)=23(−i+j+12k)⋅(23i+13j+23k)=23(−23i⋅i+13j⋅j+13k⋅k)=23(−23+13+13)=0.✓

content.problem:
The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{2}{{t}^{2}+2}\cdot q(t).
$$

Find the principal normal vector at the point where $t=1$, if 

$$
\begin{aligned}q(1)=-i+j+\frac{1}{2}k,\,{q}^{′}(1)=j+k.\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
First, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2}{{t}^{2}+2}\cdot q(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2}{{t}^{2}+2})\cdot q(t)+\frac{2}{{t}^{2}+2}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(q(t)) \\  & =-\frac{4t}{({t}^{2}+2)^{2}}\cdot q(t)+\frac{2}{{t}^{2}+2}\cdot {q}^{′}(t) \\  \\ {T}^{′}(1) & =-\frac{4(1)}{({1}^{2}+2)^{2}}\cdot q(1)+\frac{2}{{1}^{2}+2}\cdot {q}^{′}(1) \\  & =-\frac{4}{9}(-i+j+\frac{1}{2}k)+\frac{2}{3}(j+k) \\  & =\frac{4}{9}\,i+\frac{2}{9}\,j+\frac{4}{9}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(1)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{4}{9})}^{2}+{(\frac{2}{9})}^{2}+{(\frac{4}{9})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{16}{81}+\frac{4}{81}+\frac{16}{81}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{36}{81}} \\  & =\frac{6}{9} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(1)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve at the point where $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(1) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(1)}{‖{T}^{′}(1)‖} \\  & =\frac{\frac{4}{9}\,i+\frac{2}{9}\,j+\frac{4}{9}\,k}{(\frac{2}{3})} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\,i+\frac{1}{3}\,j+\frac{2}{3}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Note that when we find the scalar product of $T$ and $N$ at the point where $t=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1)\cdot N(1) & =\frac{2}{3}q(1)\cdot (\frac{2}{3}\,i+\frac{1}{3}\,j+\frac{2}{3}\,k) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}(-i+j+\frac{1}{2}k)\cdot (\frac{2}{3}\,i+\frac{1}{3}\,j+\frac{2}{3}\,k) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}(-\frac{2}{3}\,i\cdot \,i+\frac{1}{3}\,j\cdot j+\frac{1}{3}\,k\cdot k) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}(-\frac{2}{3}+\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{3}) \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given by T(t)=24+t⋅q(t). Find the principal normal vector at the point where t=0, if q(0)=⟨1,3⟩,q′(0)=⟨1,0⟩.

a
 13⟨2,1⟩
b
12⟨−1,3⟩
c
 12⟨−1,1⟩
d
 12⟨3,−1⟩
e
12⟨3,−1⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: By the product rule, T′(0)=−(1/8)q(0)+(1/2)q′(0)=⟨3/8,−√3/8⟩. Its magnitude is √3/4. Thus N(0)=T′(0)/‖T′(0)‖=(1/2)⟨√3,−1⟩, which is option e.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{2}{4+t}\cdot q(t).
$$

Find the principal normal vector at the point where $t=0,$ if 

$$
\begin{aligned}q(0)=⟨1,\sqrt{3}⟩,\,{q}^{′}(0)=⟨1,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
First, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2}{4+t}\cdot q(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2}{4+t})\cdot q(t)+\frac{2}{4+t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(q(t)) \\  & =-\frac{2}{{(4+t)}^{2}}\cdot q(t)+\frac{2}{4+t}\cdot {q}^{′}(t) \\  \\ {T}^{′}(0) & =-\frac{2}{{(4+0)}^{2}}\cdot q(0)+\frac{2}{4+0}\cdot {q}^{′}(0) \\  & =-\frac{1}{8}⟨1,\sqrt{3}⟩+\frac{1}{2}⟨1,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{8}(-⟨1,\sqrt{3}⟩+4⟨1,0⟩) \\  & =\frac{1}{8}⟨3,-\sqrt{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(0)‖ & =\frac{1}{8}\sqrt{{3}^{2}+(-\sqrt{3})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{8} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(0)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve at the point where $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(0) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(0)}{‖{T}^{′}(0)‖} \\  & =\frac{\frac{1}{8}⟨3,-\sqrt{3}⟩}{(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4})} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨\sqrt{3},-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Note that when we find the scalar product of $T$ and $N$ at the point where $t=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(0)\cdot N(0) & =\frac{1}{2}q(0)\cdot \frac{1}{2}⟨\sqrt{3},-1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨1,\sqrt{3}⟩\cdot \frac{1}{2}⟨\sqrt{3},-1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(1\cdot \sqrt{3}+\sqrt{3}\cdot (-1)) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{3}) \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{2}{4+t}\cdot q(t).
$$

Find the principal normal vector at the point where $t=0,$ if 

$$
\begin{aligned}q(0)=⟨1,\sqrt{3}⟩,\,{q}^{′}(0)=⟨1,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
First, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2}{4+t}\cdot q(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2}{4+t})\cdot q(t)+\frac{2}{4+t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(q(t)) \\  & =-\frac{2}{{(4+t)}^{2}}\cdot q(t)+\frac{2}{4+t}\cdot {q}^{′}(t) \\  \\ {T}^{′}(0) & =-\frac{2}{{(4+0)}^{2}}\cdot q(0)+\frac{2}{4+0}\cdot {q}^{′}(0) \\  & =-\frac{1}{8}⟨1,\sqrt{3}⟩+\frac{1}{2}⟨1,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{8}(-⟨1,\sqrt{3}⟩+4⟨1,0⟩) \\  & =\frac{1}{8}⟨3,-\sqrt{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(0)‖ & =\frac{1}{8}\sqrt{{3}^{2}+(-\sqrt{3})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{8} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(0)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve at the point where $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(0) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(0)}{‖{T}^{′}(0)‖} \\  & =\frac{\frac{1}{8}⟨3,-\sqrt{3}⟩}{(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4})} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨\sqrt{3},-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Note that when we find the scalar product of $T$ and $N$ at the point where $t=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(0)\cdot N(0) & =\frac{1}{2}q(0)\cdot \frac{1}{2}⟨\sqrt{3},-1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨1,\sqrt{3}⟩\cdot \frac{1}{2}⟨\sqrt{3},-1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(1\cdot \sqrt{3}+\sqrt{3}\cdot (-1)) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{3}) \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$
